title: Tenant Network Evacuation and Traffic Cordon Playbook
author: Amina Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook defines a deterministic process for performing a tenant-scoped network evacuation (traffic cordon) in VPC and on-prem private deployments. It covers triggers, prechecks, traffic quiesce mechanisms, graceful KV/cache and GPU eviction, model hot-swap guidance, tenant-level quota and billing considerations, and verification. The goal is to safely isolate and/or evacuate an individual tenant with minimal collateral impact to co-located tenants and to preserve customer data integrity and compliance evidence.

Scope and when to use this playbook

Use this playbook when a single tenant or a set of tenant endpoints meets one of the following conditions:
- Confirmed data exfiltration or suspected lateral movement within tenant-controlled network segments.
- Repeated, uncontrolled noisy neighbor behavior not mitigated by quota limits.
- Customer-requested isolation for legal/forensic reasons.
- Hardware/network emergency affecting tenant's compute fabric (thermal events, NIC failures) where evacuation reduces risk of data corruption.

Do NOT use this playbook for full-cluster failovers or region-wide DR; those are covered in the regional failover runbooks.

Owners and escalation

- Primary owner: Private Deployments Oncall (team: eng-private-deployments)
- Runbook lead (responsible for execution): On-call Operator
- Secondary owner: Platform Reliability (eng-sre)
- Security escalation: Incident Response (security-and-compliance)
- Customer comms: Customer Success assigned AM

Pager and Slack channels:
- Pager duty: private-deployments-oncall@example.com
- Slack: #private-deploy-ops (primary), #security-incidents (security consult)

SLOs and allowable impact

- Evacuation target window: complete tenant cordon and eviction within 30 minutes (soft).
- Latency SLO for co-tenants: 99th percentile latency must not degrade > 20% during the operation.
- Availability SLO for co-tenants: no more than 1% error-rate increase allowed during the operation.

Pre-evacuation checklist (must verify before initiating)

1. Authorization and ticketing:
   - Approved change ticket exists and is linked to the runbook (CID).
   - Customer contact and legal hold requirements confirmed if applicable.
2. Inventory and scope:
   - Tenant ID(s), project names, CIDR ranges, VPC/subnet IDs, and compute node IDs enumerated.
   - Map of services used by tenant (inference services, KV cache instances, tracing endpoints) exported.
3. Backups and evidence:
   - If forensics required, snapshot relevant disks and export audit logs to secure evidence bucket (see Evidence Preservation steps).
4. Capacity check:
   - Confirm spare capacity for model swap/replication on target nodes or fallback pool.
   - Validate GPU and memory headroom >= 20% for destination pool.
5. Communication:
   - Notify #private-deploy-ops and assigned AM.
   - If customer-impacting, coordinate a controlled announcement window.

Commands and quick reference

- Lock tenant route table (example, AWS CLI):
  aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --association-id rtbassoc-xxxxxxxx --route-table-id rtb-xxxxxxxx

- Example iptables cordon rule on host (evict control-plane ingress):
  sudo iptables -I INPUT -s 10.12.0.0/24 -j DROP  # cordon tenant CIDR

- Graceful eviction (runtime controller):
  ./runtimectl tenant drain --tenant-id tenant-123 --grace-period 120  # waits for in-flight tokens

- KV cache flush and checkpoint: (example Redis sentinel command)
  redis-cli -h redis-tenant-01 BGSAVE && redis-cli -h redis-tenant-01 CLIENT PAUSE 12000

Step-by-step evacuation procedure

1) Initiate authorization and snapshot evidence (5–10 minutes)
   - Operator confirms ticket and legal constraints.
   - If forensics requested: snapshot volumes, collect kernel logs, export audit and network flow logs to evidence bucket (aws s3 cp /var/logs/tenant-123 s3://evidence/tenant-123/).

2) Apply a soft traffic cordon (2–3 minutes)
   - Add ingress deny for tenant CIDR in edge-load-balancer ACLs to stop new external inbound sessions while allowing existing sessions to complete.
   - In VPCs, add a route with blackhole next-hop for tenant subnets (or use NACL deny rules depending on network design).
   - Announce to internal channels: "Soft cordon applied — no new external connections allowed for tenant-123."

3) Trigger runtime graceful drain (5–10 minutes)
   - runtimectl tenant drain --tenant-id tenant-123 --grace-period 120
   - This signals the model servers to stop accepting new tasks from the tenant and allows in-flight requests to finish. The runtime releases KV cache references and writes checkpoints per the KV migration policy.

4) Evict model-backed worker pods / processes in phases (10–15 minutes)
   - Phase A: Evict non-critical jobs (batch, long-running analytics) from tenant-allocated nodes.
   - Phase B: Evict GPU-bound model workers. Use the model-hot-swap template to instantiate fallback quantized model variants in the fallback pool if customer requires continuity.

5) Drain and detach storage, then apply hard cordon (5 minutes)
   - Ensure disks have completed snapshots and detach volumes from nodes.
   - Replace iptables rules to DROP all tenant traffic on compute hosts to prevent lateral movement.
   - Update service discovery so tenant endpoints resolve to 127.0.0.1 (or equivalent blackhole).

6) Post-evacuation verification (5–10 minutes)
   - Verify no active connections from tenant CIDR (netstat/lsof).
   - Confirm KV cache checkpoint timestamps and that no cache writebacks are pending.
   - Confirm model servers removed tenant mappings (runtimectl tenant status --tenant-id tenant-123 => STATE=evacuated).

7) Escalation and rollback path
   - If co-tenant impact exceeds SLOs, perform immediate rollback: remove cordon rules and reattach services in reverse order.
   - Rollback command: runtimectl tenant restore --tenant-id tenant-123 --from-snapshot s3://recovery/tenant-123/snap-YYYYMMDD

Evidence preservation and chain-of-custody

- For any legal/forensic scenarios follow these steps exactly: snapshot EBS volumes (or equivalent), export kernel and application logs to an immutable bucket with object lock, and record operator actions in the change ticket.

Example evidence checklist table (plain text)

| Item | Command / Location | Owner | Retention |
|------|--------------------|-------|-----------|
| Disk snapshot | aws ec2 create-snapshot ... | Oncall Operator | 90 days (legal may extend) |
| Audit logs | aws s3://evidence/tenant-123/audit | Security | 365 days |
| Network flows | netflow-collector:/flows/tenant-123 | Networking | 90 days |

Model hot-swap guidance

- When tenant requires uninterrupted inference: instantiate a lighter-weight quantized model shard in the fallback pool instead of moving original model artifacts. This reduces GPU memory requirements and startup time.
- Use the following template to request a hot-swap:
  runtimectl model deploy --model-id model-xyz --profile quantized-8bit --pool fallback-pool --expect-ready 60
- Validate sample completions against baseline prompt set before routing production traffic to the fallback model. Record evaluation metrics (perplexity, top-k match) in the change ticket.

Automation and safety checks

- Automated prechecks (CI task) must pass before any operator-initiated cordon: health of fallback pool, required quota, and snapshot availability.
- Feature flag: tenant-evacuation-autobots (default: off) — only enable in controlled drills.

Metrics and observability to monitor during operation

- Per-tenant request rate, error-rate, and queue depth (dashboard: tenant-ops/evacuation-live)
- GPU utilization and memory pressure of fallback pool
- Number of in-flight KV connections (target: 0 after graceful drain)
- Audit events: cordon.apply, tenant.drain.start, tenant.drain.complete

Postmortem and restoration checklist

1. Confirm customer requirements for restoration (legal hold, approval).
2. Re-run restore command from last consistent snapshot; validate data integrity.
3. Reattach services: model servers, caches, tracing exporters in reverse order of eviction.
4. Run a targeted test suite (5–10 smoke prompts + embedding checks) before marking tenant as active.

Sample smoke test (shell):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.private.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"fallback-quant-8bit","input":"smoke: hello"}' | jq '.status, .latency'

Appendices

A. Configuration snippets
- Autoscaler safety policy (YAML):
  policy: |
    name: tenant-evacuation-safety
    min_pool_headroom: 0.2
    max_bulk_eviction_rate: 0.1

B. Quick decision matrix
- If noisy neighbor and < 5% request-share: prefer quota throttle and alert owner.
- If noisy neighbor > 20% or evidence of exfiltration: initiate evacuation playbook.

C. Post-run audit items
- Attach all snapshots and logs to the change ticket.
- Owner writes a one-page incident summary and uploads to the postmortem repository.

Contact

If unsure, call the private deployments oncall and include the change ticket ID in all communications.
